I couldn't write these notes. Both attempts to load the source pages failed. The first was stopped by a tool usage limit, and the second was blocked because I had no tool calls left this turn. That means I haven't read any pages from enduringword.com, biblehub.com, studylight.org, preceptaustin.org or the other approved sites.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point and leave out anything I couldn't find. Since I found nothing, I have no verse notes to give you, with or without sources. I haven't written any from memory, because that would break those rules.

These are the pages I planned to read:
- **Traditional reading:** enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-18/ and preceptaustin.org/psalm-18-commentary
- **Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit and others:** biblehub.com/commentaries/psalms/18-26.htm through 18-50.htm
- **Catholic and Patristic:** Augustine's exposition at newadvent.org/fathers/1801018.htm. The Vulgate counts this psalm as Psalm 17, so sources in that numbering may list it that way.
- **Modern scholarship:** netbible.org notes on Psalm 18 and bibleodyssey.org
- **Tradition-specific views:** spurgeon.org (Treasury of David), wesley.nnu.edu (Wesley's notes), gty.org, ligonier.org and others, mainly on vv. 26, 35 ("Your gentleness exalts me"), 43–45 and 49–50

If you ask again in a new turn, I'll start with these pages, fetching them one at a time to stay under the limit, and write the notes verse by verse with a URL for each point.
